convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I said something cruel. I think about it every day. Let's move."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Fritz doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I wasn't a physical therapy aide. I was a tattoo artist. I thought if you believed that, you'd trust me faster. I'm sorry. Or I'm supposed to be." Quiet. Real.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Burdock — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
"Me? I laughed yesterday and it scared me — the sound of it. Like my body remembered something my head hadn't approved. Laughter's a mutiny. A good one."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Violet owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I keep turning over the last thing Violet said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the meadow edge, west of the creek and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about White Noise last night — what to even CALL it. 'Ugly-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."

"About that question — You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before? No pressure, though."
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."

"Hm. Still on what you did with your hands."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"

"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.

"Still on what they want."
